newsitem.title: MEXICO: Televisa shareholders approve changes to board.
newsitem.headline: Televisa shareholders approve changes to board.

text.p: Shareholders at Mexican media company Grupo Televisa SA on Wednesday approved the naming of Emilio Azcarraga Jean as chairman of the board, sources close to the company told Reuters.
Guillermo Canedo White, the outgoing chairman, was named president of the company's Executive Committee, a newly formed body, said the sources, who were at the shareholders' meeting.
"The assembly unanimously approved the naming of Emilio Azcarraga Jean as chairman of the board of directors," said one source, who added that the meeting took only 20 minutes.
He said the executive committee would be responsible for managing the company's operations and finances but would ultimately answer to the board of directors.
"The result should kill all rumors of a split between groups of control in the company," said the source.
In the past days, rumors have swirled in Mexico that rival groups of shareholders were vying for control of the firm, the largest entertainment company in the Spanish-speaking world.
The sources added that several prominent Mexican businessmen were named to the Executive Committee, including Claudio X. Gonzalez, head of Kimberly-Clark de Mexico.
